concept.title: Circular dynamics: centripetal is a net-force role, not a new force
concept.inferential_jump: The inward acceleration requirement v^2/r fixes only the net radial component m v^2/r; tension, friction, gravity, normal force, or combinations may supply that resultant, so 'centripetal force' must not be added as another interaction.
entry_assumptions: Can identify tangent velocity and inward acceleration in elementary uniform circular motion.
Can draw a chosen-body FBD and apply Newton II along a declared axis.

teaching_path.action: Hold speed constant and compare tangent velocity arrows at nearby points before showing any force.
teaching_path.why_valid: Direction change establishes nonzero inward acceleration without invoking a force label.

teaching_path.action: Quantify the inward acceleration as a_r=v^2/r.
teaching_path.why_valid: REL-CIRC-RADIAL-ACCELERATION is the gate-owned curvature relation.
teaching_path.output: a_r = v^2/r; for v=4 m/s and r=2 m, a_r=8 m/s^2.

teaching_path.action: Choose one body and draw only real interactions, then declare inward-positive radial/tangential axes.
teaching_path.why_valid: Force ownership and sign choice must precede Newton-II components.

teaching_path.action: Set the signed real-force radial resultant equal to m v^2/r.
teaching_path.why_valid: REL-CIRC-NET-RADIAL-FORCE is Newton II applied to the established radial acceleration.
teaching_path.output: Sigma F_r=m v^2/r without an extra Fc arrow.

teaching_path.action: Switch among string, flat-curve friction, and gravity-supplied mechanisms while holding the same radial requirement.
teaching_path.why_valid: The force type can change while the centripetal role remains the net radial resultant.

teaching_path.action: Remove the string interaction and predict the immediate inertial path.
teaching_path.why_valid: Without inward tension, instantaneous velocity remains tangent at the cut event.
teaching_path.output: initial post-cut path tangent, not radially outward.

teaching_path.action: At vertical-circle top and bottom, re-declare inward and write the corresponding signed radial equations.
teaching_path.why_valid: Gravity keeps its physical downward direction while the radial positive direction changes around the circle.

teaching_path.action: At the top impose the just-taut boundary T=0 to derive the minimum top speed.
teaching_path.why_valid: A string cannot push, so negative tension signals failure of the taut-string model.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Tension plus an additional centripetal force both point inward.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: A mass moves in a horizontal circle on one string. Which horizontal force arrows belong on its inertial-frame FBD?
misconceptions.repair: Draw the string tension only; 'centripetal' names the role of the net inward component.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: A cut string makes the object fly radially outward.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: At the instant a circular-motion string is cut, which direction does the object initially move?
misconceptions.repair: Keep the instantaneous tangent velocity; removing tension removes inward acceleration, not the tangent velocity.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Static friction on a flat curve always equals mu_s N.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: At a low speed on a high-friction flat curve, must friction already be at its maximum?
misconceptions.repair: Compute m v^2/r first and compare that demand with the static bound.

correspondence.in_words: The instantaneous velocity follows the tangent, not the radial axis.
The radial acceleration points toward the centre and has magnitude v^2/r in the uniform model.
The signed sum of real radial force components supplies the required inward resultant m v^2/r.
The radial axis is re-declared toward the centre at each selected point.

relation_checks: Doubling v at fixed r quadruples a_r.
Doubling r at fixed v halves a_r.
At fixed m,r, doubling v quadruples required inward net force.
Setting T=0 gives the just-taut boundary relation.
For positive speed, T must exceed mg in this ideal bottom state.
Mass cancels from the boundary result.

exit_task.prompt: A 2 kg mass moves at 4 m/s in a horizontal circle of radius 2 m on a string. Draw the inertial-frame horizontal FBD and find the required inward net force. Then state the immediate path if the string is cut.

answer.summary: Only tension is drawn horizontally. The required inward net force is m v^2/r=16 N, so tension supplies 16 N in the simplified horizontal model. If the string is cut, tension vanishes and the mass initially follows the tangent.
reasoning: Velocity is tangent while acceleration is inward.
Draw the real string interaction only.
The cut removes inward tension; instantaneous tangent velocity remains.
answer.check: Do not add a second Fc arrow; that would double-count the required inward resultant.
